summary.name: Understanding error budget overspend - part one
summary.one_liner: A 2018 Google Cloud Platform blog post (part of the CRE Life Lessons series) explaining how to diagnose and respond when a service consistently overspends its SLO error budget.
keywords: how to fix error budget overspend
use_cases: Diagnosing where error budget is being spent
Deciding whether to adjust an SLO target
Negotiating reliability with a dependency owner
Deciding when to slow feature releases after an outage
Documenting the tradeoff between user happiness and reliability
summary.what_it_does: The article explains that an SLO sets allowed downtime (an error budget), for example 43 minutes per 30 days at 99.9% availability. It describes how to analyze budget spend day by day and attribute it to causes such as binary releases, steady intermittent application failures, major outages from configuration pushes or overload, and external dependencies. It suggests checking whether an outage reflected real user pain, so the SLI or SLO target can be changed. It also covers lowering an SLO target when user metrics show little impact, and notes that business decisions may favor continued releases over budget. The post is part one of a two-part series.
notable: Attributes error budget spend to root causes such as releases, application failures, major outages, and dependencies
Argues SLO targets should be documented with the data used to set them
Part one of a two-part series; links to related CRE posts on building SLOs and consequences of SLO violations
caveats: Written as a 2018 blog post; it is conceptual guidance, not a tool or product
Describes principles only and does not give step-by-step implementation details
Part two, which covers keeping a positive error budget balance, is referenced but not included on this page
